classification.difficultyReason: Structurally identical to p28-q9: a ratio of two masses in scientific notation, then the number of atoms in a given mass by division. It has the same demand with different numbers (2.4 kg rather than 1 kg adds a trivial step).

content.prompt: The mass of a carbon atom is $1.9945\times10^{-26}$ kg and the mass of a hydrogen atom is $1.6735\times10^{-27}$ kg.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate, correct to 4 s.f., the ratio of the mass of a carbon atom to the mass of a hydrogen atom (i.e. how many times as heavy is a carbon atom compared to a hydrogen atom?)

answer.short: $11.92$ times as heavy. Divide the carbon mass by the hydrogen mass.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}\text{Mass ratio}&=\frac{1.9945\times10^{-26}}{1.6735\times10^{-27}}\\\text{Mass ratio}&=\frac{1.9945}{1.6735}\times10^{1}\\\text{Mass ratio}&\approx11.92\quad(4\text{ s.f.})\end{align*}$$
A carbon atom is approximately $11.92$ times as heavy as a hydrogen atom.

children.label: b
children.prompt: How many carbon atoms are there in 2.4 kg? Answer in scientific notation to 4 s.f.

answer.short: $1.203\times10^{26}$ atoms. Divide $2.4$ kg by the mass of one carbon atom.
